# Queued extraction M0 fixtures

All content is fabricated, public test data. No service, account, source URL or
credential is used to generate it. These files are test inputs, never runtime
assets. `manifest.json` freezes original SHA-256, expected normalized text/hash,
character counts, locations or a safe failure code on the original M0 baseline.
The expected text is independently specified from the labels used to author the
files; it is not generated by invoking the extractor under test.

| Original | Baseline contract |
| --- | --- |
| `readable-100.pdf` | 100 individually labelled pages in source order |
| `mixed-scan.pdf` | Readable page followed by a real embedded image; whole input fails `unsupported_scan` |
| `blank-pages.pdf` | Five pages; only pages 2 and 4 contribute text/locations |
| `all-blank.pdf` | Two legitimate blank pages; whole input fails `no_text` |
| `structured.docx` | Two sections, distinct headers/footers, a table and Unicode body; headers follow the body in current extraction |
| `fenced.md` | BOM, CRLF, Unicode, link, real and fenced headings; current location parser also matches the fenced heading |
| `plain.txt` | Unicode, CRLF and trailing CR normalize without changing text |
| `multipart.md` | More than 128 KiB of Unicode Markdown; the existing project publisher creates its logical parent/parts |

Rebuild with the repository's pinned `pypdf`/`python-docx` environment:

```sh
python tests/fixtures/evidence/pipeline/generate.py
python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_ingestion_pipeline_baseline.py
```

PDF objects, DOCX core dates and ZIP entry timestamps are deterministic. The
manifest is deliberately not rewritten by the generator: changes require review
of original bytes, independently expected text and compatibility consequences.
M0 captures existing limitations; future structural parsing must deliberately
version its changed location expectations while preserving canonical full text.
